# QSO Predictor

> A free, open-source desktop tactical assistant for FT8 and FT4 amateur
> radio operators. Reconstructs the DX station's perspective using PSK
> Reporter spot data so you can see the pileup *they're* hearing, find
> frequencies clear at *their* location, and confirm propagation paths
> before calling. Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux alongside WSJT-X or
> JTDX via UDP integration, or with the browser-based FT8web client via
> a local WebSocket connection. A built-in Diagnostics suite ("the
> Doctors") passively checks the whole station — system clock vs NTP,
> app configs, the UDP decode chain, serial/CAT ports and adapter
> chips, OS power-management traps, and (on Windows) the audio path
> behind "RX works but TX is silent" — and produces one shareable
> markdown report designed to be pasted into a forum thread or an LLM
> chat. Nothing is changed, opened, or transmitted by the diagnostics.
> Advisory only — the operator keeps full control of the radio.

QSO Predictor is written by Peter Hirst (WU2C), licensed under GPLv3.
Built in Python with PyQt6. Distribution: free GitHub releases (Windows
zip, signed-and-notarized macOS dmg, source for all platforms) and a
Microsoft Store listing (Windows only, easiest install).

The app does not collect, transmit, or store any personal data. It reads
local WSJT-X/JTDX log files, optionally receives decode data from an
FT8web browser client over a local WebSocket (off by default), subscribes
read-only to the public PSK Reporter MQTT stream, and fetches space
weather from NOAA SWPC. No telemetry. No tracking.

## Primary documentation

- [User Guide](https://qsop.wu2c.net/user-guide/): Installation, configuration, and how to use each feature of the app.
- [Home page](https://qsop.wu2c.net/): Project overview, installation options, key features.

## Integration guides

- [Integrations overview](https://qsop.wu2c.net/integrations/): Running QSO Predictor alongside the rest of the FT8 ecosystem.
- [Run WSJT-X with GridTracker, JTAlert, and your logger at the same time](https://qsop.wu2c.net/integrations/wsjtx-udp-multicast/): Why only one app receives WSJT-X UDP decodes, and the two fixes — multicast (recommended) and daisy-chain forwarding — with exact settings and troubleshooting. Applies to WSJT-X and JTDX, with or without QSO Predictor.
- [QSO Predictor + GridTracker](https://qsop.wu2c.net/integrations/gridtracker/): Both apps on one UDP stream — multicast and daisy-chain configurations, verification steps, troubleshooting.
